live_prose.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the tile sign-act (4:1-4:3) from the lying and food-rationing sign-acts (4:4-4:17) as two units. How the sign-acts of chs 4-7 divide is an open question, and the 4:3/4:4 seam is its strongest form. The mark on the verse before this cut is weighed as corroboration for the alternative: on the rival's far face the witness records a samekh after oshb:Ezek.4.3 (single-witness), and that verse closes on the sign-act colophon א֥וֹת הִ֖יא לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.4.3), “This shall be a sign to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.4.3), standing verse-final. On the rival's near face the candidate onset oshb:Ezek.4.4 carries no formula whatever: MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness, no verse of ch 4 belongs to the counted messenger, utterance, recognition or word-event formula classes, the chapter's only counted device verses being the son-of-man address at 4:1 and 4:16 and the year-word non-datelines at 4:5-4:6. The colophon is not a close-role formula - oshb:Ezek.4.3 is neither an utterance-formula verse (sweep: 81 verses) nor a member of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses) - and the addressee is unchanged across the seam, 2ms imperatives standing to the prophet on either side. A ve'attah inside an open unit begins a sub-unit only when the addressee changes or the verse before it ends on a verse-final close-role formula; neither holds here, and a mark by itself never supplies that close. The rival is therefore paragraph-grade, held on those grounds, and the samekh is disclosed for the alternative it corroborates rather than for this row. live_prose.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.11.14 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, the strict word-event formula (one of the book's 39 strict-form onsets), opens an oracle addressed to the exiles rather than to the courtyard men of Ezek.11.1-11.13 — an addressee-class shift inside the vision, from the Jerusalem claimants (oshb:Ezek.11.15, which the WEB renders “This land has been given to us for a possession.” (web:Ezek.11.15)) to “your brothers… the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.11.15) in exile. The witness records a pe after MT 11:13 (single witness), at the seam this unit opens on at 11:14. Close: oshb:Ezek.11.21 וְאֶל לֵ֧ב שִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֛ם וְתוֹעֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם לִבָּ֣ם הֹלֵ֑ךְ דַּרְכָּם֙ בְּרֹאשָׁ֣ם נָתַ֔תִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה ends with the utterance formula נאם אדני יהוה (one of the book's 81 utterance-close verses). Both sides are formula-clean: a strict word-event onset and an utterance close, the tightest formula bracket in this span. This embedded salvation oracle stands inside the still-open vision (the courtyard scene has not yet returned the prophet — that happens only at 11:22-25) but is bounded by its own onset and close formulae independent of the vision frame, so it is set as its own row rather than folded into 11:1-13 or 11:22-25.
live_prose.strongest_rejected_alternative: Holding 11:14-21 inside a single long 11:1-21 courtyard-and-oracle row, with the word-event at 11:14 disclosed only as internal texture, was weighed as an alternative reading. It was not taken because 11:14 is a strict word-event onset (not a bare transition) and the oracle's own addressee — the scattered exiles — differs from the courtyard men addressed in 11:1-13, which is enough of a class shift to justify treating it as its own formula-bounded row even while the wider vision frame stays open around it. A second rival sits inside this row and is weighed here as well: a seam at 11:16/11:17. This witness records a samekh after MT 11:15 and another after MT 11:16 (single witness), and because the witness enters each mark on the verse it stands after, both fall immediately before a verse that carries the long messenger formula כה אמר אדני יהוה — oshb:Ezek.11.16 and oshb:Ezek.11.17, two of that formula's 122 verses. Neither seam is licensed as a sub-onset, since a messenger formula opens one only if the people addressed change or the verse just before it finishes on a close-role formula. The addressee holds steady: the son-of-man address and the scattered exiles are named at 11:15 and nothing readdresses the oracle before 11:21. Nor does either preceding verse finish on a close-role formula — MEASURED on the pointed witness, MT 11:15 finishes לָ֥נוּ הִ֛יא נִתְּנָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ לְמוֹרָשָֽׁה (oshb:Ezek.11.15) and MT 11:16 finishes בָּאֲרָצ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אוּ שָֽׁם (oshb:Ezek.11.16), while in 11:16 and in 11:17 alike the messenger formula stands at the verse's head after לכן אמר rather than at its end. A mark alone cannot stand in for that verse-final formula, so the two samekhs are disclosed for the paragraph structure they corroborate within the row, and the row rests on its strict word-event onset at 11:14 and its verse-final utterance close at 11:21 (MEASURED: נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה closes MT 11:21; oshb:Ezek.11.15, oshb:Ezek.11.21).
live_prose.device_notes: Filed as salvation_oracle per the restoration promise that is the unit's burden (gather-and-return is stated here: MEASURED at oshb:Ezek.11.17, the oracle both gathers and gives the land — the consonantal skeleton carries וקבצתי אתכם מן העמים ואספתי אתכם מן הארצות and ונתתי לכם את אדמת ישראל, which the WEB renders “I will gather you from the peoples, and assemble you out of the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.” (web:Ezek.11.17) — and the “one heart… heart of flesh” (web:Ezek.11.19) promise stands alongside it, so the salvation_oracle filing rests on the device the unit actually carries); a one-sentence deviation is disclosed because the unit also carries a disputation-oracle color (the quoted Jerusalem claim at 11:15 is refuted before the promise is given), and the category is not read as free text beyond that single disclosure. No K/Q or paseq falls in this span.
